name: Apollo 11 Descent Stage
sizeComparison: Size of a two-story house (3.2 m tall)
superpower: Carried Neil Armstrong & Buzz Aldrin to become the first humans on the Moon.
funFact: The astronauts left a golden olive branch for peace and a plaque that reads: 'Here men from the planet Earth first set foot upon the Moon. We came in peace for all mankind.'
story: On July 20, 1969, the Lunar Module 'Eagle' touched down in the Sea of Tranquility with only 25 seconds of fuel left! While the top half blasted the astronauts back into space, this sturdy four-legged golden base stayed behind. Today, it still stands quietly in the lunar dust as humanity's very first monument on another world.

name: Surveyor 3 & Apollo 12
status: Historic Meetup Site at Ocean of Storms
sizeComparison: Size of a patio picnic table (3 m tall)
superpower: The only robotic lander on another world ever inspected in person by humans from a later mission!
funFact: Apollo 12 astronauts Pete Conrad and Alan Bean walked right up to Surveyor 3, clipped off its camera with bolt cutters, and brought it back to Earth for NASA scientists to study!
story: Surveyor 3 landed on the Moon in 1967 and scooped up the lunar soil to prove it was solid enough for humans to walk on. Two and a half years later, the Apollo 12 crew pulled off a pinpoint landing just 160 meters away and walked over to say hello! It proved humans could land anywhere they wanted on the Moon.

name: Apollo 15 Lunar Rover
sizeComparison: Size of a golf cart (3.1 m long, wire-mesh tires)
superpower: First electric car driven by humans on another world, with four independent 0.25-horsepower motors!
funFact: Astronauts drove the rover up to 12 km/h (7.5 mph) and did 'rooster tail' drifts in the powdery lunar soil! It was so folded up during launch that it popped open like an umbrella on the Moon.
story: Before Apollo 15, astronauts could only hike as far as their boots could carry them. This electric buggy let David Scott and James Irwin cruise 28 kilometers across giant mountain ridges and volcanic canyons. When their mission was over, they parked it facing away so its TV camera could broadcast their liftoff to kids watching back on Earth.

name: Apollo 17 Challenger & LRV
sizeComparison: Size of a dune buggy (carried 2 astronauts + 250 lbs of rocks)
superpower: Drove 36 km — the longest distance humans have ever driven on another celestial body!
funFact: Astronaut Gene Cernan accidentally snapped off the rear fender with a hammer. Dust was blinding them, so they taped 4 lunar maps together with gray duct tape to make a homemade fender!
story: Apollo 17 was humanity's final Apollo mission to the lunar surface. Gene Cernan and scientist-astronaut Harrison Schmitt drove deep into the Taurus-Littrow valley and discovered orange volcanic glass beads billions of years old. The rover still sits there today, ready for the next Artemis astronauts to visit.

name: Mars Pathfinder & Sojourner
sizeComparison: Size of a kitchen microwave (only 65 cm long, 23 lbs on Earth!)
superpower: The first wheeled rover ever to drive on another planet in human history.
funFact: On Mars, gravity is so weak that little Sojourner weighed only 9 pounds — a fourth-grader could easily lift it with one hand! It was named after heroic abolitionist Sojourner Truth.
story: When Pathfinder bounced onto Mars wrapped in gigantic airbags on July 4, 1997, it deployed a tiny 6-wheeled robotic pet named Sojourner. Planned to last just 7 days, Sojourner explored for 83 days, sniffing rocks with cartoon names like 'Barnacle Bill' and proving that robots could drive safely across Martian rocks.

name: Spirit Rover (MER-A)
status: Peacefully asleep at Home Plate, Gusev Crater
sizeComparison: Size of a golf cart with solar wings (1.6 m long)
superpower: Survived 20 times longer than planned, climbing giant rocky hills and sending 124,000 photos!
funFact: When Spirit's front wheel jammed and stopped turning, engineers drove it backwards! The broken wheel dragged in the dirt and accidentally scraped open a layer of pure white silica — proving hot springs once bubbled on Mars!
story: Spirit was designed for a 90-day sprint, but this brave robot survived for over 6 years! It scaled the peaks of the Columbia Hills, dodged swirling dust devils that cleaned its solar panels, and helped scientists realize Mars had a warm, watery, volcanic past. It sent its final salute in 2010 when winter settled over the red planet.

name: Curiosity Rover
status: Actively climbing Mount Sharp in Gale Crater
sizeComparison: Size of an SUV or mini-van (3 m long, weighs nearly 1 ton!)
superpower: Shoots a high-powered laser to zap rocks into glowing vapor from 7 meters away!
funFact: Curiosity has tiny patterned holes cut into its aluminum wheels that spell out 'J-P-L' in Morse code. Every time it rolls through the sand, it stamps secret code into Mars to help track its odometer!
story: Curiosity arrived on Mars with a thrilling 'Sky Crane' rocket backpack that lowered it gently on nylon ropes. It carries a complete chemical laboratory inside its belly! Curiosity proved that ancient Gale Crater was once a freshwater lake that had all the chemical ingredients needed for microscopic life to thrive.

name: Perseverance & Ingenuity
status: Collecting core samples at Jezero Crater
sizeComparison: Car-sized rover + a 4-pound flying drone helicopter
superpower: Drills rock cores and seals them in titanium tubes for a future rocket to bring back to Earth!
funFact: Ingenuity carried a tiny piece of wing fabric from the Wright Brothers' historic 1903 Flyer taped under its solar panel — bringing the first Earth airplane to the first Mars flying machine!
story: Nicknamed 'Percy', this rover is searching for fossilized traces of ancient alien microbes in a dried-up river delta. Under its belly, it brought Ingenuity, the very first aircraft to fly through Mars's razor-thin atmosphere. What was supposed to be a 5-flight test turned into 72 breathtaking flights across the Martian sky!
